simple.meaning: אָהַל (ʼâhal) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to tent.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 3 times in Genesis, Isaiah, beginning at Genesis 13:12. The surrounding contexts include flock, altar, land.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אָהַל (H167) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: אָהַל (ʼâhal) / H167 is traced through Genesis 13:12, Genesis 13:18, Isaiah 13:20 with source-language evidence and verse context.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Abram lived in the land of Canaan, and Lot lived in the cities of the plain, and moved his tent as far as Sodom.

majorEvents.evidenceText: Abram lived in the land of Canaan, and Lot lived in the cities of the plain, and moved his tent as far as Sodom.

timeline.evidenceText: Abram lived in the land of Canaan, and Lot lived in the cities of the plain, and moved his tent as far as Sodom.
Abram moved his tent, and came and lived by the oaks of Mamre, which are in Hebron, and built an altar there to Yahweh.
It will never be inhabited, neither will it be lived in from generation to generation. The Arabian will not pitch a tent there, neither will shepherds make their flocks lie down there.

definitions.full: H167. ahal [ אָהַל ] verb denominative tent, move tent from place to place (compare Assyrian â'ilu (?) Dl W No. 4 & Agl ) וַיֶּאֱהַל Gen 13:12 , 18 (J), compare אֹהֶל ישֵׁב (see אֹהֶל ); Pi`el Imperfect יַהֵל (contracted for יְאַהֵל ) pitch one's tent like nomad Isa 13:20 .
